column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly describes a thirty-cubit line encircling the Sea; BSB gives its circumference.
The Hebrew repeats all around and speaks of figures underneath it without separately naming the rim.
The Hebrew leaves the Sea unnamed in the first standing clause; BSB names it.
The Hebrew places two expressions of holding and containing together; BSB uses could hold.
The Hebrew uses right and left, and an active rinsing verb; BSB uses south and north and a passive.
The Hebrew uses right and left; BSB interprets these as south and north.
The Hebrew uses right and left; BSB interprets these as south and north.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the right side eastward toward the south; BSB specifies a southeast corner.
The Hebrew names bowls without separately specifying sprinkling.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew locates the capitals at the face of the pillars; BSB places them atop the pillars.
The Hebrew twice repeats he made; BSB gives a bare list.
The Hebrew explicitly says one Sea and uses underneath it; BSB repeats the Sea.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew directly makes the king the casting subject and speaks of thick earth; BSB describes commissioning casting in clay molds.
The Hebrew says the bronze’s weight was not investigated; BSB says it could not be determined.
The Hebrew directly says the Bread of the Presence was on the tables; BSB supplies a placement verb.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has blossom singular; BSB uses flowers.
The Hebrew explicitly names the entrance of the house before its doors; BSB presents the gold doors directly.
